inspection_summary: Inspected all 2,082 Python-split lines of Booker's article. The source develops a finite-height route from net zero observations and Heilbronn-character constraints to Artin holomorphy and bounded GRH checks, then supplies two complementary zero-location methods: an explicit-formula positivity optimizer and a generalized Turing count with rigorous integral bounds. It also constructs a many-value FFT algorithm for critical-line L-functions with residue, Taylor, truncation, and discretization error control, and closes the chain on S5/A5 examples. Formula extraction is imperfect but the prose, equation labels, and local derivations recover the main mechanisms; graph-only pages are not semantically recoverable from the normalized text.

sections_inspected.label: Front matter and abstract
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Title metadata and a source-authored overview of the group criterion, zero locators, rigorous FFT evaluation, and numerical tests.

sections_inspected.label: 1. Introduction
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Frames the effective Artin-holomorphy problem, its relation to bounded RH verification, the two zero-computation routes, and the generic analytic L-function contract.

sections_inspected.label: 2. A criterion for verifying Artin's conjecture
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Turns uncertain net-zero counts into virtual-character constraints, defines almost monomiality, proves closure properties, audits finite groups, and separates Artin holomorphy from the weaker bounded-RH condition.

sections_inspected.label: 3. Locating zeros via the explicit formula
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Uses coefficient-zero duality, compact Fourier support, positivity, and quadratic optimization to produce rigorous zero-exclusion intervals under RH.

sections_inspected.label: 4. Turing's method
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Generalizes zero counting for L-functions with simple zeros and derives explicit upper and lower bounds for the integrated argument term.

sections_inspected.label: 5. Rigorous Computation of L-functions: transform and FFT setup
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Recasts many critical-line evaluations as one Fourier/Mellin transform and discretizes it with Poisson summation and controlled aliasing.

sections_inspected.label: 5.1. Computing G
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Builds residue-series evaluation, certified tails, derivative recurrences, reusable Taylor tables, and a second convolutional FFT.

sections_inspected.label: 5.2. Complexity
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Explains the damping/precision/coefficient tradeoff and square-root analytic-conductor scaling.

sections_inspected.label: 5.3. Asymptotics
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Derives effective large-u, Dirichlet-series truncation, transform-alias, and sampling-tail bounds needed for rigorous computation.

sections_inspected.label: 6. Numerical results
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Instantiates the representation relations, coefficient pipeline, independent zero diagnostics, interval arithmetic, FFT evaluation, and Turing closure on S5/A5 fields.

sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Bibliography and author address inspected and excluded from semantic units.

accepted_units.title: Artin holomorphy as a positive certification problem
accepted_units.why_material: The source distinguishes falsifying Artin's conjecture by finding a pole from certifying holomorphy when the only critical-strip representation is a Brauer ratio, where a denominator zero and a tiny nearby pole-zero cancellation cannot be resolved naively.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the odd/even two-dimensional comparison and the ineffective theorem motivating a finite-height criterion.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Low to moderate: the conceptual obstruction is prose-grounded; names and the eigenvalue typography should be checked against the PDF if quoted exactly.

accepted_units.title: Coupling Artin holomorphy, bounded RH, and complementary zero locators
accepted_units.why_material: It explains why Turing's method alone normally presupposes holomorphic irreducible factors, how the new criterion can remove that circularity, and why explicit-formula estimates and rigorous many-value evaluation play different roles.
accepted_units.context_note: This is the source's architectural overview for Sections 3–5 rather than a result imported from later detail.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Low: the mathematical roles and dependencies are explicit in prose.

accepted_units.title: Generic analytic contract for the L-functions under computation
accepted_units.why_material: The Euler product, completed function, functional equation, analytic conductor, possible-pole polynomial, and Ramanujan-type bound specify exactly which later zero-count and numerical arguments are reusable beyond Artin L-functions.
accepted_units.context_note: Retains the whole assumption packet because later symbols Q, chi, P, theta, gamma, and Lambda depend on it.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High: several displayed formulas are text-layer degraded; the prose and equation numbers are recoverable, but exact symbolic reuse requires PDF verification.

accepted_units.title: Net-zero counts cannot by themselves certify local holomorphy
accepted_units.why_material: Argument-principle counts for numerator and denominator reveal only zeros minus poles in a neighborhood, so finite numerical uncertainty cannot rule out a pole masked by a nearby zero.
accepted_units.context_note: This local-identifiability failure is the problem that the character-theoretic criterion repairs.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Moderate: the contour formula is formula-dependent, while the obstruction is clear in prose.

accepted_units.title: Heilbronn characters convert analytic orders into monomial inequalities
accepted_units.why_material: Factoring Dedekind zeta and monomial Artin L-functions turns every possible local order pattern into a virtual character nonnegative on monomial representations, and confines individual zeros and poles to zeros of the Dedekind zeta function.
accepted_units.context_note: The unit links analytic zero orders to finite-dimensional character data.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Moderate to high: products, inner products, and the Heilbronn-character definition depend on displayed formulas whose labels remain legible.

accepted_units.title: Runtime simplicity hypothesis becomes character indecomposability
accepted_units.why_material: Assuming distinct simple irreducible zero patterns only as a checked runtime hypothesis, an observed net zero for one representation is certified when its character cannot split into two nonzero virtual characters nonnegative on all monomial representations; the central point requires a parity-aware variant.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes conditions (2.7), (2.8), and Definition 2.1 so the generic and central-point criteria are not conflated.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High: exact quantifiers and the central-point sum are formula-dependent, though the surrounding prose fixes their meaning.

accepted_units.title: Almost monomiality as cone proximity and indecomposability
accepted_units.why_material: The source reframes the criterion geometrically: the dual nonnegative region cut out by monomial characters must leave irreducible character rays indecomposable. It also identifies central multiplicity as a distinct practical limitation of sign-change counting.
accepted_units.context_note: The missing figure is described sufficiently by the prose; the final paragraphs explain why the central condition is kept separate.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Moderate: the figure itself is not present as structured data, but its cone interpretation is recoverable from text.

accepted_units.title: Almost monomiality survives quotients and products with monomial groups
accepted_units.why_material: The proposition and proof show how the certification property transports through common group constructions using lift/descent, Frobenius reciprocity, and tensor-product inner products.
accepted_units.context_note: Both cases of Proposition 2.2 are retained because they use different transport mechanisms.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Moderate to high: representation-theoretic notation is degraded in places, but the proof's logical flow is readable.

accepted_units.title: Lattice enumeration certifies A5, S5, and SL2(F3)
accepted_units.why_material: The source reduces almost monomiality to a finite integral-basis search: enumerate bounded inner-product vectors, invert the monomial Gram matrix, and test the remaining inequalities; the same finite audit handles the central parity condition.
accepted_units.context_note: A5 is the worked example and GAP supplies the group data; this is computational evidence for the named finite groups.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High: vector coordinates and matrix constraints are essential and should be checked against the PDF or regenerated in GAP before reuse.

accepted_units.title: Induced information can be insufficient to expose a hidden pole
accepted_units.why_material: GL2(F3) and SL2(F5) defeat the optimistic generalization: even after adding known non-monomial induced cases, certain virtual-character decompositions allow a pole to hide at a zero of the six-dimensional factor.
accepted_units.context_note: This is an explicit boundary of the criterion, not a failure of numerical precision alone.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High: the decisive twelve spanning vectors and failing decompositions are formula/table dependent.

accepted_units.title: Adjoint-square bridge and a weaker route to bounded RH
accepted_units.why_material: Passing an icosahedral representation to its three-dimensional adjoint square suggests an effective converse-theorem route, while the local character condition for RH allows bounded verification even when full Artin holomorphy is unavailable.
accepted_units.context_note: The source separates an in-principle analytic bridge, a practical discriminant bottleneck, and the weaker condition (2.11).
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Moderate to high: the conceptual bridge is prose-grounded; exact virtual-character inequalities are formula-dependent.

accepted_units.title: Compactly supported coefficient data probes the zero spectrum
accepted_units.why_material: Weil's explicit formula converts finitely many Euler/Dirichlet coefficients into weighted zero sums; under RH, nonnegative band-limited test functions turn this identity into a localized spectral probe.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes both the coefficient definition and the positivity caveat so the method is not mistaken for an unconditional RH certificate.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High: the explicit formula and Fourier conventions are symbol-heavy and require scan verification for exact implementation.

accepted_units.title: Zero exclusion as constrained quadratic minimization
accepted_units.why_material: A finite trigonometric-square family makes the positive zero sum a positive-definite quadratic form; minimizing it subject to h(t0)=1 gives a computable quantity below one only when t0 is not a zero ordinate.
accepted_units.context_note: This is the reusable bridge from an abstract infimum to matrix inversion and rapid evaluation at many targets.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High: basis functions, support parameters, and the threshold depend on displayed formulas.

accepted_units.title: Resolution cost, close-zero sensitivity, and diagnostic use of the explicit formula
accepted_units.why_material: The uncertainty principle ties coefficient range to local zero density, exceptionally small gaps can increase cost, and the RH-dependent method is positioned as a fast low-zero locator and cross-check rather than the final unconditional certificate.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the self-dual cost reduction and the explicit comparison with Turing's method.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Moderate: asymptotic typography is degraded, but the qualitative scaling and methodological role are recoverable.

accepted_units.title: Generalized Turing counting from phase plus argument
accepted_units.why_material: The functional equation folds an argument-principle contour onto the critical half-plane, decomposing the net zero count into a computable gamma phase Phi and the argument term S; simple critical-line zeros are then observed by sign changes.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the non-self-dual warning that only differences in the chosen counting function are canonical.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High: the contour identities, definitions of S/Phi/N, and branch conventions are formula-dependent.

accepted_units.title: Integrated step-function bounds recover the missing zero-count offset
accepted_units.why_material: Left- and right-endpoint brackets around observed sign changes give one-sided counting functions; integrating them and bounding the mean of S isolates the integer N(t0), so only endpoint neighborhoods need precise zeros while the interior needs sign changes.
accepted_units.context_note: This is the operational core of Turing's method and states the precision-window tradeoff.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High: inequalities (4.7)–(4.10) determine the certified directions and integration intervals.

accepted_units.title: Functional equation plus pole clearing yields a uniform strip bound
accepted_units.why_material: A symmetric auxiliary function and the Phragmen-Lindelof principle propagate boundary bounds across the strip; multiplying by shifted pole polynomials repairs holomorphy when L has poles.
accepted_units.context_note: The pole-free and pole-bearing cases are both needed to understand why the rational P-factors appear later.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High: the exact strip, gamma/conductor factor, and shifted P-ratio are equation-dependent.

accepted_units.title: Uniform gamma, conductor, and pole logarithmic-derivative control
accepted_units.why_material: Under a separation condition at height t, explicit Stirling estimates bound the logarithmic derivatives of the gamma factor, analytic conductor, and pole polynomial uniformly in the spectral parameters.
accepted_units.context_note: These estimates feed both the integrated-S theorem and FFT sampling-tail bounds.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High: constants, ranges, and the separation hypothesis are formula-dependent; prose alone is insufficient for implementation.

accepted_units.title: Paired-zero comparison controls the lower logarithmic integral
accepted_units.why_material: A strip inequality for an integrated logarithmic ratio, proved by asymptotics, maximum principle, real-axis calculus, and a bounded computation, supplies the device that controls nearby-zero contributions in the lower bound.
accepted_units.context_note: This is Lemma 4.3 as a proof mechanism; the source explicitly labels its final bounded-region check computational.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High: the exact inequality and domain are displayed-formula dependent.

accepted_units.title: Ramanujan bounds sandwich L and its logarithmic derivative by zeta envelopes
accepted_units.why_material: Pairing Euler factors produces explicit upper and lower zeta-based envelopes for both |L| and the real logarithmic derivative, converting local coefficient bounds into global computable constants.
accepted_units.context_note: The proof uses the pairing assumption from the generic L-function contract.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High: definitions of z_theta and Z_theta and inequality orientations must be verified from the displayed equations.

accepted_units.title: Explicit two-sided bound for the integrated argument term
accepted_units.why_material: Theorem 4.5 combines the strip bound, gamma estimates, zeta envelopes, a Hadamard product over functional-equation-paired zeros, and Lemma 4.3 to bound the integral of S with an explicit conductor main term and controlled error.
accepted_units.context_note: The long span is retained because upper and lower bounds use different mechanisms and only their combination closes Turing's integer count.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Very high: extraction degrades several integrals and constants; the conceptual proof is recoverable, but exact numerical certification requires the original PDF.

accepted_units.title: One Mellin transform enables many rigorous critical-line values
accepted_units.why_material: Instead of evaluating a two-parameter Cauchy-integral family pointwise, the source Fourier-transforms the damped completed L-function, expands its Dirichlet series through a single kernel G, and uses Poisson summation to obtain an FFT pair.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes pole residues and the discretization parameters A, B, and q because they determine the exact transformed data.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Very high: Fourier normalization, damping sign, residues, and Poisson-summation indices are formula-dependent.

accepted_units.title: Reality symmetry reduces transform sampling to a half-grid with certified tails
accepted_units.why_material: Conjugate symmetry reduces the FFT input range, while large-shift asymptotics and a separate critical-line bound account for transform aliasing and time-domain wraparound.
accepted_units.context_note: This short unit is the error-accounting interface between the FFT identity and later Lemmas 5.4–5.5.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High: the shifted sums and parameter placement are equation-dependent.

accepted_units.title: Contour shifting gives a computable residue series for the kernel G
accepted_units.why_material: The Mellin kernel becomes a sum over gamma-factor poles; grouping equivalent shifts and propagating polar coefficients by recurrence yields a tail bounded by the last computed pole block and eventual factorial decay.
accepted_units.context_note: The Galois gamma expansions illustrate the general residue machinery, while Lemma 5.1 supplies the rigorous stopping rule.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Very high: residue orders, recurrences, and the tail hypothesis require exact formula verification.

accepted_units.title: Derivative recurrences and Taylor caches turn G into reusable family infrastructure
accepted_units.why_material: A shift in one gamma parameter computes derivatives of G, enabling certified local Taylor models that are reusable across every L-function with the same archimedean parameters; binning Dirichlet coefficients then converts evaluation at all samples into convolutions handled by another FFT.
accepted_units.context_note: This unit links analytic recurrence, approximation error, family reuse, and algorithmic convolution.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Very high: the derivative identity, Taylor remainder, bin definitions, and convolution indices are formula-dependent.

accepted_units.title: Damping trades precision against coefficient range at square-root conductor scale
accepted_units.why_material: Choosing eta near one slows decay enough to reach height T but raises coefficient/precision demands; after this tradeoff, the dominant coefficient count is of square-root analytic-conductor size and the FFT supplies many values at near-linear mean cost.
accepted_units.context_note: The source explicitly treats the best constant as an empirical parameter choice later illustrated in Section 6.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Moderate to high: the qualitative tradeoff is prose-grounded, while the asymptotic exponents are formula-extraction sensitive.

accepted_units.title: Effective large-u control of G from stationary phase and contour shifting
accepted_units.why_material: The source states the stationary-phase shape of G and derives a less sharp but fully effective contour-shift bound using Holder and explicit gamma estimates, making the large-shift FFT terms certifiable.
accepted_units.context_note: Lemma 5.2 is retained with its proof because its constants feed every later error estimate.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Very high: the extracted stationary-phase formula and definitions of delta, nu, mu, K, and X need original-formula verification.

accepted_units.title: Coefficient growth plus kernel decay certifies Dirichlet-series truncation
accepted_units.why_material: A polynomial coefficient bound and the effective G estimate make the omitted tail monotone after an explicit threshold, so an incomplete-gamma-style integral bounds every term beyond M.
accepted_units.context_note: The remark records how coarse global coefficient bounds can be replaced by tighter range-specific constants.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Very high: thresholds, exponents, and products in Lemma 5.3 are formula-dependent.

accepted_units.title: Two tail lemmas close both sides of FFT discretization
accepted_units.why_material: Lemma 5.4 sums shifted transform samples using kernel decay and pole residues; Lemma 5.5 sums shifted critical-line values using the functional-equation strip bound, together certifying aliasing in both Fourier domains.
accepted_units.context_note: These are distinct error channels but form one closure mechanism for the discrete FFT computation.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Very high: sign conditions, beta, E, geometric factors, and residue denominators require exact symbolic verification.

accepted_units.title: S5 character relations reduce global conjectures to selected nonvanishing checks
accepted_units.why_material: For the worked S5 field, monomiality and explicit direct-sum relations identify which Artin factors are already holomorphic and reduce the remaining Artin/RH certification to zero isolation and nonvanishing of a small collection of compound L-functions.
accepted_units.context_note: The source reports no counterexamples only in the tested range |t|<=100; this is bounded computational evidence.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High: exact representation sums, conductors, and factor names must be preserved.

accepted_units.title: Parameter selection balances coefficient availability, damping, and interval precision
accepted_units.why_material: The worked computation chooses eta by comparing the largest truncation error with the expected function size, determines how far beyond the target height Turing bounds require evaluation, and assigns interval arithmetic to the rigorous downstream stages.
accepted_units.context_note: The reported timings and decimal precisions are source-specific implementation evidence, not universal complexity claims.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High: numerical exponents and the extracted coefficient-count typography should be checked against the retained PDF before reproduction.

accepted_units.title: Dedekind-zeta ratios handle ramification while Frobenius classes scale coefficient generation
accepted_units.why_material: Brauer-style zeta ratios provide local factors at exceptional primes, while unramified Frobenius conjugacy classes are recovered from low-degree factorization data modulo p, yielding essentially linear-time coefficient generation.
accepted_units.context_note: The two routes are complementary: the general computer-algebra path resolves ramification and the finite-field path supplies volume.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High: the exact zeta ratios and factorization notation are formula-dependent.

accepted_units.title: Explicit-formula zero spikes cross-check coefficients and expose conductor-dependent density
accepted_units.why_material: The low-zero estimator yields unit-height spikes at plausible ordinates, agrees with the known zeta zero quoted by the source, and visibly tracks conductor/degree; because the explicit formula is coefficient-sensitive, this supplies an independent integrity check before the rigorous FFT/Turing pass.
accepted_units.context_note: The local-factor and lowest-zero tables are source-specific evidence, not a proof of the later bounded claims by themselves.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Very high: graph data are not embedded here and the extracted tables/formulas need source-image verification for exact values.

accepted_units.title: Certified local G models feed the main FFT evaluation
accepted_units.why_material: The implementation precomputes high-precision Taylor models of G with a stated remainder, spends most effort on binned coefficient moments, and then makes the actual L-value FFT fast while choosing A and B so the sampling-tail bound is negligible.
accepted_units.context_note: The section heading is extraction-damaged, but the prose and references to (5.16), (5.18), and Lemma 5.5 recover the workflow.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High: several powers and parameter values are text-layer ambiguous and require the original PDF for exact reruns.

accepted_units.title: Agreement of independent zero locators precedes Turing closure
accepted_units.why_material: The source compares zeros of the rigorously computed critical-line function with explicit-formula spikes, then applies Turing's method while simultaneously checking the runtime zero-isolation working hypothesis.
accepted_units.context_note: This establishes a layered validation chain: agreement is diagnostic, while the Turing count supplies the bounded completeness certificate.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Moderate: the interpretive prose is recoverable, but the underlying plots are graphic-only in the normalized text.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: From uncertain local counts to certified Artin holomorphy
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Net-zero neighborhoods become holomorphy certificates when Heilbronn-character nonnegativity and finite character-cone indecomposability rule out every hidden zero-pole decomposition.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The source still requires the distinct/simple zero pattern to succeed as a checked runtime hypothesis, and the finite-group criterion fails for some groups.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Bounded RH can be certifiable without full Artin holomorphy
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: A weaker virtual-character obstruction, combined with a complete Turing count of simple critical-line zeros, can certify bounded RH for a Dedekind zeta function even where the stronger almost-monomial condition does not certify every Artin factor.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: This is finite-height, representation- and zero-isolation-dependent evidence; it is not an unconditional global RH result.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Explicit formula proposes and diagnoses; Turing certifies completeness
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: The coefficient-driven explicit formula rapidly localizes low zeros, tunes parameters, and catches coefficient errors, while direct critical-line evaluation plus Turing's mean-argument bound certifies that no zeros were missed.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The positive-minimization locator assumes RH for the factor being probed, so its agreement is a diagnostic rather than the final independent certificate.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Single-kernel FFT with a closed rigorous error budget
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Recasting many L-values through one Mellin kernel permits cached local approximations and FFT convolution, while residue tails, Taylor remainders, Dirichlet truncation, transform aliasing, and time-domain wraparound are each bounded explicitly.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: Exact certified implementation depends on recovering formula constants and conventions from the original PDF, not the degraded normalized text alone.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Family reuse follows archimedean representation rather than individual L-function identity
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Once G and its derivatives are certified for a gamma-parameter tuple, the expensive analytic cache can be reused across arithmetic-family members, leaving only source-specific Dirichlet coefficients and pole data to change.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: Reuse is restricted to identical gamma parameters and compatible normalization; ramified local factors still need individual computation.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: End-to-end bounded S5 evidence chain
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Character relations select the necessary compound L-functions, scalable Frobenius computation supplies coefficients, explicit-formula spikes audit them, interval-certified FFT values find sign changes, and Turing counting closes completeness while checking zero isolation.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The reported outcome is tied to the listed fields, implementation parameters, and tested height |t|<=100; it does not establish either conjecture globally.

within_source_saturation: Saturated after 35 accepted units spanning every distinct source-supported mechanism, obstruction, criterion, analytic estimate family, algorithmic transformation, and computational validation step. Unselected material is limited to source furniture, acknowledgements, previews represented later, routine algebra internal to accepted theorem spans, graph-only extraction, and bibliography.

Further units would duplicate the selected Artin-character criterion, explicit-formula locator, Turing completeness certificate, FFT/error machinery, or S5 execution chain, or would rely on graph-only extraction and bibliographic matter rather than additional recoverable mathematical content.
